![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The CLI execution block only sets a non-zero exit code (`process.exitCode = 1`) when the validator status is `'fail'`. However, according to the general rules, CLI validation scripts must exit with a non-zero exit code for any validation status other than a successful pass (such as `'blocked'`) to prevent blocked runs from passing silently in CI/CD pipelines. Please update the condition to check if the status is not `'pass'`.

```suggestion
  if (artifacts.validatorResult.validator_status !== 'pass') {
    process.exitCode = 1;
  }
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. CLI validation scripts must exit with a non-zero exit code for any validation status other than a successful pass (such as 'fail' or 'blocked') to prevent blocked or failed runs from passing silently in CI/CD pipelines.
</details>
Fixed in 899fd6db7: the CLI now exits non-zero for any validator_status other than pass, so blocked validator runs cannot pass silently.

Fixed in 899fd6db7: added a fail-closed regression that injects a critical input diagnostic and asserts validator_status fail, critical_input_diagnostics_present, and the failed no_critical_input_diagnostics check.
